checks: Solving the two line intercepts gives A=Br/(B+r) and a=bt/(b+t). The four core areas are AB/2, at/2, ab/2, Ar/2. The three caps sum sectors (4,5,0), (0,1,2), and (2,3,4) respectively. Their boundary rays have zero area.

Core inclusion on the remaining two sectors yields x>=P and y>=Q, including equality. Multiplication gives UV=PQ. The fraction bound is immediate at or above 1/2. Below 1/2 the two bounds on x-y give Z<R. Swapping U and V while replacing xi by p/xi leaves Z unchanged. With U>=V, the inequality (U-V)xi<V-Up yields U<Q and then 0<P<R<=T<Q.

Independently cleared the positive denominator in Z-Z_0. Its coefficients in xi are P^2(Q-U)^2, 2PQ(Q-U)(P-U), and Q^2(P-U)^2, giving the stated square. S<P+Q follows by expanding (Q-U)(Q-V)>0. These facts give 0<Z_0<=Z<R.

The largest cap ratio decreases in x before the crossing and increases after it, where the derivative has numerator y+S-Z>0. The crossing y+T-Z is positive. At the crossing the derivative in y has numerator R-Z>0. Replacing y by Q and then Z by Z_0 gives the displayed lower bound in the correct directions.

At Q=1 the denominator is obtained by multiplying the prior positive denominator by (1-P)T. Differentiating gives the factor P(1-P)(1-T)(3T+1). At T=s and P=s^2 the common factor s(1-s) cancels. The difference from 8/17 is (3s-1)^2/[17(s^2+5s+2)]. Exact rational subtraction gives 56/4743>0 above 128/279.
